deep.reconstruction:
This page has no computations. It is a heavily corrected prose draft of the passage that became §5 of Riemann's Inaugural-Dissertation (1851), 'Grundlagen für eine allgemeine Theorie der Functionen einer veränderlichen complexen Größe'. It introduces a bounded surface T spread over the plane A, now called a (bordered) Riemann surface. The previous page continues the same draft, with winding points of order m-1 and §6, Green's theorem.

(1) Top lines, struck through. Riemann pictures the image of a region under a map. In the image plane B, two 'arms' of the image can meet along part of the boundary, so the image overlaps itself.

(2) First paragraph, crossed out with large diagonal strokes. Let z (equivalently w) take continuously varying values on a bounded piece of the plane A. Then its image ('Bild') in B is again a bounded, finite piece. However, if z takes the same value at different points, different parts of this image coincide. Viewing the dependence this way therefore forces one to consider a bounded surface region whose parts lie on top of one another. This is the motivation for the surface T: the image of a domain under a non-injective map covers parts of B several times.

(3) Second attempt, crossed out. 'Let S denote a finite connected region of the plane A...' A point may be represented several times, and different parts of the region coincide depending on the kind of connection.

(4) Retained version, close to the printed §5:
- 'For the following investigations we restrict the variability of the quantities x, y to a finite connected region.'
- We do this 'with the Einkleidung' (way of dressing the idea) that a connected bounded surface T is spread over the plane A. In one part of this plane, different parts of T may coincide.
- Assumption: superposed sheets are never joined along a line. This excludes a fold (Umfaltung) of the surface and a splitting of T into two superposed sheets.
- Modern statement: T → A is a local homeomorphism away from isolated points, plus the boundary.

(5) The sheet count n(p). Draw in A a line l through the part covered by T. Where l does not meet the boundary of T, the number of superposed sheets must be the same on both sides of l. Riemann does not write this out; the following is my gloss, consistent with the printed text. The count is locally constant off the boundary. It changes by +1 or -1 when the boundary is crossed (outside to inside, or the reverse). Hence n(p) is fixed by the position and orientation of the boundary. In modern form, n(p) is the winding number of the oriented boundary ∂T, projected to A, about p.

(6) Continuation of sheets across l. Label the sheets on the left of l as a_1,...,a_n and those on the right as a_1',...,a_n'. Each sheet a_i must continue into some sheet a'_{σ(i)}, and this correspondence persists along l as long as l does not meet the boundary.
- At a point q of l the correspondence may jump: a sheet a_1 continues into a sheet different from the one it continued into before.
- Going round q then carries a_1 into a_2, a_2 into a_3, and so on. After m steps the cycle closes.
- Such a q is the 'Windungspunkt (m-1)ter Ordnung' that the previous page describes. Several cycles at the same q (orders m_1-1, m_2-1, ...) correspond to the cycle decomposition of the local monodromy permutation.

The final lines are fragmentary. They say a point must be excluded ('ausgeschlossen') when going round it carries one sheet into another. That fixes the definition of branch points.

What the section serves: preparing the domain T of the functions w(x+iy) on which §6 (Green's theorem) and the theory of connectivity (next page) operate.
errors: No mathematical errors. The draft is conceptual and has no derivations to check.
The rule that sheet number is constant across l and changes by ±1 at the boundary is asserted without proof. It is intuitive here, and it is also unproved in the printed text.
The non-folding hypothesis (no Umfaltung, no splitting along a line) is imposed by fiat. It is needed so that the projection is a local homeomorphism except at isolated points.

results.what: Concept of a bounded surface T spread (possibly multiply) over the plane, motivated by the self-overlapping image of a domain under a non-injective map; superposed sheets not joined along lines
results.modern_name: Riemann surface (bordered branched covering of a planar domain)

results.what: Number of superposed sheets is locally constant, changes by ±1 across the oriented boundary, hence determined by boundary position and orientation
results.modern_name: Degree / winding-number count of a covering (argument principle for the boundary)
results.usually_credited_to: Riemann 1851 in this form (degree theory later formalized by Kronecker and Brouwer)

results.what: Continuation of sheets across a line; points where the sheet correspondence permutes cyclically are winding points of order m-1
results.modern_name: Branch points and local monodromy (cycle decomposition of the monodromy permutation)

deep.surprise_reason: This is a draft of §5 of Riemann's 1851 dissertation (Riemann surfaces, sheet counting, winding points), known in its printed form. The only extra is the explicit motivation via the overlapping conformal image in B. That is of mild genetic interest, not a new result.

checkable.asserts: The image of the unit disk under w=z**2 has boundary w=exp(2it), which winds twice about 0. So the image surface over a point near 0 has 2 sheets: sheet number equals the boundary winding number.
Each interior value w=1/8 has 3 preimages under w=z**3, matching the 3-sheeted image. At w=0 the sheets meet in a winding point of order 3-1=2.
Illustrates the ±1 rule: a boundary made of a 3-fold outer loop and a reversed single inner loop gives sheet number 3-1=2 between them.

transcription_corrections: 'ein bergränzt[?] u. endlich ... Stück' should read 'ein begränztes u. endliches ... Stück'.

'{+Geschrieben auf+} [-Wir Gesprochen-] Für die folgenden Untersuchungen' is most likely a reordering of 'Wir beschränken' to 'beschränken wir'. The printed text reads 'Für die folgenden Betrachtungen beschränken wir die Veränderlichkeit der Größen x, y auf ein endliches Gebiet'.
'und dabei der Erweiterung, daß' should read 'unter der Einkleidung' (printed text: 'Wir wählen diese Einkleidung').
'die Veränderlichkeit der Größe x, y' should read 'der Größen x, y'.
'daß ein ℜ [-...-] in mehrfacher Weise' is probably 'daß ein Punkt ... in mehrfacher Weise'.
'die Abhängigkeit der Größe z von [-...-] {+von+}' probably continues 'von w' or 'von x, y', i.e. the dependence of z viewed as a mapping.
'Linie in 2 über liegenden Flächen' should read 'sich in 2 über einander liegende Flächen spaltet'.
In the sheet-labelling sentence, one side ('zur Linken') is labelled a_1...a_n and the other ('zur Rechten') a_1'...a_n'. The machine text duplicates the line.
In the second struck paragraph, 'die Abbildung zusammenfallen' refers to 'verschiedene Theile dieser Abbildung zusammenfallen' (parts of the image coincide).
